text: For my own part, I would rather be in company with a dead man, than with an absent one; for if the dead man gives me no pleasure; at least he shows me no contempt; whereas, the absent man, silently indeed, but very plainly, tells me that he does not think me worth his attention.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXXXII, to his son, London, September 22, Old Style 1749
